name: New Year's Day
desc: The world rings in the new year with fireworks and celebrations.

name: Makar Sankranti
desc: Hindu harvest festival marking the sun's transit into Capricorn.

name: Republic Day
desc: India celebrates the adoption of its constitution in 1950.

name: Women's Day
desc: International Women's Day — celebrating achievements of women worldwide.

name: Spring Equinox
desc: Day and night are equal. Spring officially begins in the Northern Hemisphere.

name: Holi
desc: Festival of colours celebrating the triumph of good over evil.

name: Dr. Ambedkar Jayanti
desc: Birth anniversary of B.R. Ambedkar, architect of the Indian Constitution.

name: Earth Day
desc: Annual event to demonstrate support for environmental protection.

name: Labour Day
desc: International Workers' Day — honouring the labour movement worldwide.

name: Summer Solstice
desc: The longest day of the year. The sun reaches its highest point in the sky.

name: Independence Day
desc: India's independence from British rule, declared on August 15, 1947.

name: Autumn Equinox
desc: Day and night are equal. Autumn officially begins in the Northern Hemisphere.

name: Gandhi Jayanti
desc: Birth anniversary of Mahatma Gandhi, father of the Indian nation.

name: Dussehra
desc: Celebrates the victory of Lord Rama over Ravana — good over evil.

name: Halloween
desc: Ancient Celtic festival of Samhain, now celebrated with costumes and candy.

name: Diwali
desc: Festival of Lights — one of the most celebrated festivals in the world.

name: Guru Nanak Jayanti
desc: Birth anniversary of Guru Nanak Dev Ji, founder of Sikhism.

name: Winter Solstice
desc: The shortest day of the year. The sun is at its lowest point in the sky.

name: Christmas
desc: Celebrates the birth of Jesus Christ. Observed by over 2 billion people.

name: New Year's Eve
desc: The last night of the year — celebrated with countdowns and fireworks.
